subject.title: [Bug]: CLI relay exits silently with code 1 when session lane is blocked — no timeout or busy error surfaced

question: Should Gateway-backed CLI same-session lane waits become terminal `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` busy results for all CLI-origin dispatches, and what exit-code contract should that result use?
rationale: The source fix shape is clear, but the proposed behavior changes the user-visible delivery contract for blocked CLI dispatches and the issue discussion explicitly leaves the exit-code choice to maintainers.

options.title: Adopt terminal busy for CLI
options.body: Return a structured lane-busy result for CLI-origin dispatches, render actionable stderr/JSON output, and choose a distinct or documented exit code before merge.

options.title: Only add stderr on existing failure
options.body: Keep the existing nonzero failure shape and add a clear message, avoiding a stronger delivery-contract change but giving scripts less structured signal.

options.title: Keep queueing semantics
options.body: Reject terminal busy behavior and instead improve timeout diagnostics only, leaving queued execution behavior intact for blocked same-session CLI dispatches.

recommendation.title: Adopt terminal busy for CLI
recommendation.body: Return a structured lane-busy result for CLI-origin dispatches, render actionable stderr/JSON output, and choose a distinct or documented exit code before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the Gateway-backed CLI relay and is the best available routing candidate for the CLI user-facing contract decision.
